subject: Science
title: Science Exam 6
topic: Health & Lifestyle · Periodic Table · Investigative skills
intro: AQA Higher style. You may use a calculator. Read each question carefully: if it asks for two things, give two. Write full sentences for the longer answers.

questions.q: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.ms: Carbohydrates.

questions.q: Name the substance used to test a food for lipids (fats), and give the positive result.
questions.ms: Ethanol (1); a cloudy white layer / emulsion forms when poured into water (1).

questions.q: A student has a solution made from an unknown food. Describe how she could test the solution for starch and for protein. Give the positive result for each test.
questions.ms: Starch: add a few drops of iodine solution (1), turns blue-black (1). Protein: add copper sulfate and sodium hydroxide solution (Biuret) (1), turns purple (1).

questions.q: A student adds Benedict's solution to a food sample to test for sugar. What must she do next?
options: Heat it in a water bath
questions.ms: Heat it in a water bath. Positive result: orange-red.

questions.q: Explain the difference between malnutrition and a deficiency. Give a named example of a deficiency.
questions.ms: Malnutrition: not eating a balanced diet, so too much or too little of some nutrients (1). Deficiency: a lack of one particular vitamin or mineral (1). Named example (1): lack of iron causes anaemia / lack of vitamin C causes scurvy / lack of calcium or vitamin D causes weak bones (rickets).

questions.q:
Yassin eats a portion of chips. The chips contain starch and fat.
Describe how the starch and the fat are digested and absorbed as the food passes through the digestive system. Name the organs in order and the enzymes involved.
questions.ms: Level 3 (5-6): organs in the correct order with the right enzymes, and absorption explained. Level 2 (3-4): most organs in order and at least one enzyme correct. Level 1 (1-2): some organs or enzymes named. Points: mouth, teeth chew food into smaller pieces and salivary glands add carbohydrase (amylase), which starts breaking starch into sugars; oesophagus carries food to the stomach; stomach churns food (physical digestion) with acid; small intestine: the pancreas adds carbohydrase to finish breaking starch into sugar and lipase to break fats into fatty acids and glycerol; bile from the gall bladder breaks fat into small droplets; small molecules are absorbed through the small intestine wall into the blood; large intestine absorbs water; rectum stores faeces, which leave through the anus.

questions.q: Name the enzyme that breaks down lipids (fats).
questions.ms: Lipase.

questions.q: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder. It is not an enzyme. Suggest how bile helps the digestion of fats.
questions.ms: Bile breaks fat into small droplets (1), giving a bigger surface area for lipase to work on, so fats are digested faster (1).

questions.q: Explain why alcohol is called a depressant, and give two long-term effects of drinking large amounts of alcohol.
questions.ms: It slows down the body's reactions / nervous system (1). Any two (1 each): liver damage (cirrhosis), brain damage, stomach ulcers, heart disease, reduced fertility.

questions.q: Cigarette smoke contains carbon monoxide. Explain why smokers often get out of breath more quickly than non-smokers.
questions.ms: Carbon monoxide stops the blood carrying as much oxygen (1), so less oxygen reaches the cells/muscles for respiration (1). (Also accept tar clogging the alveoli so less oxygen is absorbed.)

questions.q: Which element is in Group 7 and Period 3 of the periodic table?
questions.ms: Chlorine (Cl). Group = column, period = row.

Astatine is below iodine in Group 7. Predict its colour and its state at room temperature. Use the data to explain your predictions.
questions.ms: Black / very dark colour (1); solid (1); because the colour gets darker and the melting point increases going down the group, so astatine's melting point is above 114 °C (1).

questions.q: Compare how reactivity changes going down Group 1 with how it changes going down Group 7. Give one example of evidence from a reaction for each group.
questions.ms: Group 1: reactivity increases going down (1); e.g. potassium reacts more violently with water than sodium or lithium (lilac flame) (1). Group 7: reactivity decreases going down (1); e.g. chlorine displaces bromine from potassium bromide, but bromine cannot displace chlorine (1).

questions.q:
Bromine water is added to potassium iodide solution. The solution turns brown.
Name the element that is displaced (pushed out) in this reaction.
questions.ms: Iodine. Bromine is more reactive than iodine, so it displaces it: bromine + potassium iodide → potassium bromide + iodine.

questions.q: Iodine solution is added to potassium chloride solution. Explain why there is no reaction.
questions.ms: Iodine is less reactive than chlorine (1), so it cannot displace chlorine from the compound (1).

questions.q: Helium is a Group 0 element used to fill party balloons. Give two properties of helium that make it suitable for this use.
questions.ms: Any two (1 each): very low density / lighter than air, so the balloon floats; unreactive (full outer shell), so it does not catch fire or react; it is a gas at room temperature.

questions.q:
A student investigates how temperature affects how quickly the enzyme amylase breaks down starch. Every 10 seconds she takes a drop of the mixture and tests it with iodine. She records the time when the iodine no longer turns blue-black.
Name the independent variable, the dependent variable, and one control variable.
questions.ms: Independent: temperature (1). Dependent: time taken for the starch to be broken down / for the iodine to stop turning blue-black (1). Control, any one (1): volume or concentration of starch, volume or concentration of amylase, pH, same drop size, same 10 second interval.

She tests temperatures of 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 °C. Which type of graph should she draw?
questions.ms: Line graph, because temperature is a continuous variable. (Bar charts are for categoric data.)

questions.q: Testing only every 10 seconds makes the times less accurate. Suggest one improvement to the method and explain how it would help.
questions.ms: Improvement (1): test more often, e.g. every 5 seconds / use a colorimeter / a timer started by the same person. Explanation (1): so the end point is found more precisely, giving more accurate times. (A reason alone, with no change to the method, scores 0.)
